description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Dependency-Check fixture whose one defective dependency reports no location at all. Every value was derived by reading the fixture together with the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. Read rejection_class first -- the class this fixture actually produces is absent_path, not the unresolvable_path its filename says, and that section derives the class from paths.py rather than from the slug.
rules: No user-specified rule governs this file. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', which is the complete document; AAP 0.7 and AAP 0.10.2 say the same. Enterprise best practice applies in their place, held to the AAP's own bar: hand-verify rather than record a run, reject rather than infer, and state an absence rather than omit it. This file exists because of AAP 0.6.1, AAP 0.6.2 and AAP 0.9.4, not because of a rule.
reference_case_for: the count unit at dependency granularity -- one defective dependency carrying TWO vulnerabilities yields TWO rejections, because the unit is dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] and not dependencies[]
the two archive-member shapes side by side: a container inside the scan root, and a container outside it whose ../ segments are preserved rather than normalized

the classification order being load-bearing rather than cosmetic -- the second rejected record would have been the only row in the fixture to increment severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version, and step 4 rejects it before step 5 and severity are ever reached

fixture.line_ending: LF, with a trailing newline and no CR anywhere
fixture.derived_from: oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/dependency-check.json (sha256 53fb2fa91725148f1b33df951f95e8ee01ef98ec62bebb10b73bd541bf10de68), the positive sibling this tree already carries
derivation: the ui-test/package-lock.json dependency's filePath was emptied: '/opt/spark-src/ui-test/package-lock.json' became ''. Everything else on that dependency -- isVirtual, fileName, md5, sha1, sha256, evidenceCollected, packages[] and both vulnerabilities (CVE-2020-11023 and CVE-2020-11022) -- is byte-identical to the positive fixture's entry. It sits at index 2 here and at index 5 there.

two dependencies present in the positive fixture were dropped: jquery.dataTables.min.js and d3-flamegraph.min.js. They exercise coordinate levels 1 and 4 and the float-representation path, none of which this fixture is about.

two virtual archive-member dependencies were added at indices 5 and 6: a Guava POM inside a Spark JAR under the scan root, and a Guava POM inside a JAR in the local Maven repository, which is outside the root.
reportSchema, scanInfo (all four dataSource timestamps) and projectInfo are byte-identical to the positive fixture, and through it to harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json.
fixture.captured_provenance: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated per dependency instead of claimed for the file. Envelopes captured verbatim from the raw artifact: indices 0, 1 and 7. Envelopes authored in the positive sibling and carried here: indices 2 (with the filePath emptied), 3 and 4. Envelopes authored here for the first time: indices 5 and 6. Every packages[] and every vulnerabilities[] array in this shape is authored, as the positive sibling's own fixture block records -- the raw artifact carries 32 dependencies with zero vulnerabilities and zero packages, so no excerpt of it can exercise a single field of this adapter's row builder.
fixture.authored_shapes_follow: Dependency-Check 13.0.0's own report members, as verified against the raw artifact and against the field names harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py reads: source, name, severity, unscored, cvssv2.score, cvssv3.baseScore, cvssv4.baseScore, cwes[], description, notes, references[], vulnerableSoftware[], packages[].id and the isVirtual/evidenceCollected pair a virtual dependency carries.
fixture.archive_shape_provenance: The concatenated-member convention the two archive dependencies exercise -- the member joined onto the container with a '/' and no separator of any kind -- is recorded in harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py's module docstring as measured on this provisioning's own tool, quoting the same Guava-POM-inside-spark-network-common coordinate. It is NOT present in harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json: that artifact's 32 dependencies are all vendored web assets, and zero of their filePath values carry a '.jar/' segment. Stated rather than implied, because a reader who assumed these two rows were captured would be wrong about where the shape came from.
fixture.member_existence_corroborated: Both archive coordinates name a member that really exists. /opt/spark-src/common/network-common/target/spark-network-common_2.13-4.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar (3344544 bytes, 2238 entries) and /root/.m2/repository/com/google/guava/guava/18.0/guava-18.0.jar (2256213 bytes, 1719 entries) each contain META-INF/maven/com.google.guava/guava/pom.xml, verified by reading the archive directories. That does not change the path kind or the in_scope field -- an archive member is a non-filesystem coordinate either way -- and it is recorded because a fabricated member would have made these two rows untestable against anything.
fixture.re_derivation_trigger: These rows are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256 above makes visible.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- not SARIF, since the document carries neither a version of '2.1.0' nor a runs array, and the native detector keys on the reportSchema/scanInfo/dependencies triple this shape carries
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here. This document is a well-formed Dependency-Check report; its defect is one dependency, not its shape, and a test asserting a shape failure against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py and is not restated as an expectation of this fixture.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each in-scope row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations, and each out-of-scope row records why it matched none.

resolution_context.root_dependence: Every filePath in this artifact is filesystem-absolute and carries the root as a literal prefix, so these rows are stated for the root the fixture's own paths are under -- /opt/spark-src, the value harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json records as spark_src. They are not root-independent in the way an already-root-relative uri is. No row's path field is absolute and none retains that prefix.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the dependency-check entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.path_base_evidence: The runner builds one absolute --scan argument per allowlist directory (18 in a single invocation, invocations_per_run 1), so dependencies[].filePath is filesystem-absolute under the scan root and the resolution is a straight relativization.
resolution_context.working_directory: /opt/spark-src -- equal to the scan root, and deliberately NOT the path base: the tool reports absolute paths because it was handed absolute --scan arguments, not because of where the process ran.
resolution_context.path_basis: absolute-relativized-to-root on the four tree_file rows; archive-member-serialized on the two archive rows
resolution_context.path_kinds_present: tree_file on 4 rows, archive_member on 2, outside_root on none
resolution_context.why_outside_root_is_zero: The Maven-repository coordinate resolves to ../../root/.m2/... and so does sit outside the root, but normalize.paths.path_kind_for tests for the archive separator FIRST, so a member inside a container outside the root is classified archive_member rather than outside_root. Both kinds are non-filesystem coordinates and both take in_scope false, so the discriminator changes which counter moves and nothing else. Recorded because a reader tallying outside_root would otherwise expect 1.
resolution_context.start_line: null on every row, and deliberately so rather than by omission. Dependency-Check reports at dependency granularity -- a vulnerable component, not a line of code -- and this artifact carries no line information in any member, at any depth. Synthesising one would be inference. It is also why no reject-dependency-check-non-integer-start-line fixture exists: there is no start_line in this shape for a non-integer to occupy, so that rejection condition is unreachable for this adapter and its absence is a fact rather than a gap.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: Present on all six rows. For this shape an unformable coordinate is a rejection rather than a null field, so a row reaching the dataset always carries one; that rejection belongs to reject-dependency-check-no-package-coordinate.json.
resolution_context.count_unit: dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] -- one vulnerability is one record, whatever the dependency around it does

rejection_class.expected_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_ABSENT_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, spelled 'absent_path' there and quoted rather than paraphrased here.
derivation: the defective dependency's filePath is the empty string '' (fixture pointer /dependencies/2/filePath), not a path that resolves somewhere unwanted and not a path in a form the resolver cannot read

paths.py documents REJECT_ABSENT_PATH as covering 'the record carries no path field, or carries an empty one', and REJECT_CLASS_DESCRIPTIONS repeats it -- an empty value is that class by the module's own definition

paths.resolve_recorded_path tests `value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip())` as its FIRST branch and returns REJECT_ABSENT_PATH there, before any base, archive or relativization logic runs
dependency_check.prepare_file_path returns an empty value untouched ('if not normalised: return PreparedPath(value=file_path)'), so the resolver sees the empty string exactly as the artifact wrote it
the adapter's step 4 returns whatever paths.py classified, verbatim and unreworded, which is what makes the class paths.py's decision rather than the adapter's
rejection_class.filename_says_unresolvable_path: The fixture's slug, and therefore this file's, is 'unresolvable-path'. The class it produces is absent_path. Both are correct in their own terms and the difference is stated here rather than resolved by force: AAP 0.5.4 enumerates the rejection condition as one item -- 'An unresolvable or absent path' -- so the fixture slug took the first half of that condition's name while paths.py assigns the second half as the class. The fixture exercises the path-rejection condition this adapter can actually produce, which is what AAP 0.9.4 asks for; only the label differs.
rejection_class.why_unresolvable_path_is_unreachable_for: Not a property of this fixture but of the tool's recorded base. runner-metadata.json records path_base.kind 'filesystem_absolute' for dependency-check, and ToolPathBase.base_for_relative returns the recorded base value for that kind -- only bytecode_class, per_section_target and none return None. So every branch of resolve_recorded_path that yields REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH is closed: an absolute filePath relativizes, a relative one resolves against /opt/spark-src, an archive reference with a relative container resolves against the same base, and the kind is not 'none'. The path-family classes this adapter can reach are therefore absent_path (None, empty or whitespace-only) and malformed_record (a non-string filePath, or an archive reference that cannot be serialized).
rejection_class.what_would_have_to_change_for_unresolvab: The runner metadata would have to record a different path_base.kind for dependency-check -- 'none', or a kind with no base -- which is a fact about the provisioned runner and not something a fixture may assert. Editing runner-metadata.json to force the class would fabricate the provisioning, and AAP 0.3.2 forbids runner reconfiguration in either direction. So this expectation records the reachable class rather than manufacturing the unreachable one.
rejection_class.the_error_this_prevents: Writing 'unresolvable_path' here to match the filename would put a test in this tree that fails against a correct adapter, and the likeliest repair would be a widened rejection class or a special case in paths.py -- both of which would blur the one distinction the class vocabulary exists to keep: a record that names no location at all, versus a record that names one nothing can express.

rejection_boundary.statement: A record that names no location is a rejection. A record that names a location the scope does not cover, or one that is not a plain file in the tree, is a KEPT row with in_scope false. This fixture carries both sides on purpose, because getting the boundary wrong in the strict direction would reject a large fraction of a real artifact -- reading the contents of a JAR is exactly what this tool does.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: path is one of only two never-absent fields in the twelve-field schema, the other being severity_norm: emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS carries both, and emit.validate_rows raises on a null in either. A record with no location therefore has nothing to put in the field, and AAP 0.5.4 is explicit that such a record is rejected and counted rather than guessed into a field.

not_a_rejection.expected: the tool's normal convention on this provisioning; relativizing it is the adapter's job
not_a_rejection.evidence: All seven dependencies that report a path report an absolute one, because the runner passes 18 absolute --scan arguments. Reading absoluteness as a defect would reject every row this tool can ever produce.

not_a_rejection.case: a path outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: dev/package-lock.json (row 2) and docs/Gemfile.lock (row 3). Both exist in the pinned tree, both are legitimately reachable by a dependency-oriented scanner, and neither matches any glob. AAP 0.9.3 keeps them and AAP 0.8.3 is explicit that an individual out-of-glob coordinate never establishes a wrong scan root.

not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row serialized <container-relative-to-root>!<member>, ! the single separator, in_scope false, counted in non_filesystem_paths
not_a_rejection.evidence: Row 4's container is inside the root; row 5's is outside it and its ../ segments are PRESERVED rather than normalized, per the SARIF 2.1.0 errata amendment to section 3.10.2 that paths.py implements for every shape. Both take in_scope false through ResolvedPath.in_scope, which applies the non-filesystem rule before any glob is tested -- so a member such as core/src/main/x.jar!org/apache/Foo.class cannot match core/src/main/** on its segments alone.

rejection_boundary.the_three_lockfiles_and_why_only_two_app: The pinned tree's three out-of-glob lockfiles are dev/package-lock.json, ui-test/package-lock.json and docs/Gemfile.lock; all three exist on disk and the positive sibling carries a row for each. Only two of them are rows HERE, and the reason is the fixture's construction rather than an omission: ui-test/package-lock.json is precisely the dependency whose filePath was emptied to create the defect, so its two vulnerabilities are the two rejections. Expecting three lockfile rows and two rejections from this fixture would be expecting eleven records from an eight-record artifact.
rejection_boundary.no_guessed_path: The rejected records are rejected and counted, never given a path. Nothing in this file supplies a coordinate for them, and neither their fileName ('package-lock.json') nor their md5/sha1/sha256 is read as one. The fileName alone would have been ambiguous in any case -- two package-lock.json files exist in the pinned tree -- which is exactly why inferring from it is forbidden rather than merely discouraged.
rejection_boundary.hashes_without_a_path: The defective dependency is non-virtual and carries md5, sha1, sha256 and evidenceCollected alongside its empty filePath. That combination is synthetic and is named as such: the point of it is that a record can look complete in every other respect and still name no location, and the adapter must classify on the path field rather than on how populated the envelope looks.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of dependencies[].vulnerabilities[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction, summing len(vulnerabilities) over dependencies[]
counts.raw_count_derivation: sum(len(d.vulnerabilities)) over the eight dependencies = 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 0. The third term is the defective dependency and the reason the rejection count is two rather than one; the last is the eighth dependency, core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json, which carries no vulnerabilities key at all.
counts.raw_count_authority: harness/lib/normalize/reconcile.py, _count_dependency_check, reached through count_records('dependency-check', doc). It builds no row, which is the whole point of it: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows satisfies the identity while testing nothing.
counts.rejection_count_unit_note: TWO, decided from the fixture rather than assumed. One dependency is defective, and a naive reading gives one rejection per defective dependency; the count unit is the vulnerability, so the defective dependency's two vulnerabilities are two records, each classified on its own and each rejected. An expectation of one rejection would also break the identity, since 8 != 7 + 1.
counts.independent_count_authority: The left side comes from reconcile.count_records and the right from the adapter's own return value, which is what makes the identity a test rather than a restatement.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason for each of the four.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = 'partial', assigned wherever an artifact yielded at least one rejection. Six of the eight records parsed and were emitted; two were rejected and counted; nothing was dropped and nothing was coerced.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): thirty-three keys in that order -- twenty-four authored, plus one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member.
counters_note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool: multi_location_records 0 -- no dependency here carries a relatedDependencies array, which is the only multi-location shape this report has; multi_valued_cwe_records 1 -- row 4 alone, whose cwes array holds CWE-552 and CWE-379; multi_valued_cve_records 0 -- no record's name yields more than one CVE identifier, since a Dependency-Check name carries at most one; non_filesystem_paths 2 -- the two archive members, which is also the whole of path_kind_archive_member.
counters_arithmetic: dependencies 8 == the eight elements of dependencies[]
dependencies_skipped_non_mapping 0 + dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array 1 == the one dependency contributing no record
rows_in_scope 2 + rows_out_of_scope 4 == rows 6 -- one measurement split, not a second count of the same thing
start_line_absent 6 == rows 6, by the policy stated in resolution_context.start_line
severity_label_present 6 + severity_label_absent 0 == rows 6; the counter asks whether a severity member is present at all, so row 2's JSON number counts as present even though its basis is a score
severity_basis_label 5 + severity_basis_cvss_score 1 == rows 6, and the other three bases are 0
package_coordinate_from_package_object_package_url 6 == rows 6, the other three levels are 0, and package_coordinate_unformable 0 because every row formed one
path_kind_tree_file 4 + path_kind_archive_member 2 == rows 6, and non_filesystem_paths 2 == path_kind_archive_member 2 + path_kind_outside_root 0

archive_references_split 2 == path_kind_archive_member 2 here, because both archive coordinates arrived concatenated and needed the separator inserted; the two are distinct measurements that happen to agree, since a filePath already carrying a '!' would be an archive member that was never split
cwe_absent 2 == rows 1 and 3; cve_absent 2 == rows 1 and 2

the eight counted records are 6 rows + 2 rejections, and no counter above counts a rejected record: a rejection at step 4 never reaches the severity, cwe, cve, coordinate, path-kind or in_scope tallies

package_coordinate_precedence.authority: AAP 0.5.4's one candidate precedence for every dependency-oriented shape, implemented by harness/lib/normalize/adapters/dependency_check.py's package_coordinate(). The four levels are exercised across this tree; oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/dependency-check.rows.json is the reference case for the precedence as a whole.

package_object_package_url.rule: a package URL on the enclosing package object -- for this shape the enclosing dependency's packages[] entries, pooled across every entry before the tiebreak is applied
package_object_package_url.note: Every row in this fixture resolves at level 2, because every dependency here carries a packages[] entry whose id is a pkg: URL. Level 1 is unreached (no record carries its own purl/packageUrl/packageURL/package_url member), and levels 3 and 4 are unreached because level 2 stops first.

package_coordinate_precedence.tiebreak: Where several candidates sit at one level the lexicographically smallest wins, over the pooled candidates of the whole level rather than within one package object -- taking the first entry's value instead would make the coordinate depend on producer order.

tiebreak_exercised_by.why: 'pkg:javascript/...' sorts before 'pkg:npm/...' because 'j' precedes 'n'. Producer order puts the npm entry first and marks it confidence LOW while the javascript entry is HIGH, so neither the array order nor the confidence field decides this: the stated lexicographic rule does, and it is the only one of the three that is reproducible.

package_coordinate_precedence.the_rejected_records_also_had_one: Both rejected records sit under a dependency carrying pkg:npm/jquery@3.7.1, so a coordinate was formable for each. Neither reaches level 2, because step 5 runs after step 4 and the path rejected first. That ordering is why package_coordinate_from_package_object_package_url is 6 rather than 8, and it is asserted rather than incidental: a coordinate counter that moved for a rejected record would mean the classification order had been reordered.
package_coordinate_precedence.unformable_belongs_elsewhere: Where no candidate can be formed at any level the field is not emitted null: for this dependency-oriented shape the record is rejected under unformable_package_coordinate. That case belongs to oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/reject-dependency-check-no-package-coordinate.json, which is why package_coordinate_unformable is 0 above.

severity_policy.authority: harness/lib/normalize/severity.py -- the case-insensitive label map, the CVSS v3.1 section 5 band table, and resolve()'s ordered precedence. Nothing is mapped or banded in the adapter.
severity_policy.label_over_score: A native label in the mapped vocabulary governs whatever the scores say; a score is consulted only where no mapped label exists. Either way the entry used is recorded -- the label, or the score with its source and version.
severity_policy.bands: 9.0-10.0 Critical, 7.0-8.9 High, 4.0-6.9 Medium, 0.1-3.9 Low, 0.0 Info. The boundaries and the first four labels are the CVSS v3.1 section 5 standard's; the standard's None band is emitted under this dataset's own label Info, which is a mapping this dataset defines and not a CVSS label. Banding is by ordered numeric comparison, never lexical.
severity_policy.severity_native_rendering: A label reaches severity_native as the literal the tool wrote, stripped of surrounding whitespace and neither case-folded nor coerced -- which is why row 1 carries lower-case 'moderate'. A numeric severity reaches it as a one-decimal rendering of the full-precision value.

label_versus_score_disagreements.label: LOW
label_versus_score_disagreements.note: A wide disagreement on one record: three CVSS blocks spanning Critical, Medium and Low beside a LOW label. An implementation reading cvssv3 -- the usual choice -- emits Critical. What the label-over-score rule changes here is which entry is recorded as having governed, and that is the checkable difference.

several_cvss_structures_on_one_record.selected: none -- the mapped label LOW governed, so no score entry was consulted
none -- the mapped label MEDIUM governed, and it agrees with cvssv3's 6.5
none -- the mapped label HIGH governed, and it agrees with cvssv3's 7.1
none -- the mapped label MEDIUM governed, and it agrees with cvssv3's 5.9

float_representation_artifact.origin: An OSS Index-sourced record carries no label and Dependency-Check renders the provider's float CVSS score into the severity field, so the float32-to-float64 representation tail reaches the artifact verbatim. The value is in the fixture exactly as written here.
float_representation_artifact.path_taken: The severity member is a JSON number rather than a mapped label, and the record carries no CVSS block at all, so the number is banded as a score in its own right. The recorded entry names source 'label' with a null version -- the value came from the severity member, not from a versioned CVSS block -- which is why this row does NOT increment severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version.
float_representation_artifact.banding: Numeric, on the full-precision value rather than on the rendered text: 5.300000190734863 bands Medium exactly as 5.3 does. Rounding to one decimal place cannot cross a band boundary at this value, and the band is never taken from the rendered text.
float_representation_artifact.no_spurious_precision: severity_native carries the one-decimal rendering, so no artifact tail reaches a text field. The full-precision value appears in this file only as a JSON number under selected_entry.score, which is where severity.py keeps it.

case_insensitivity.note: Absorbed by the case-insensitive map, whose keys are upper-case and whose lookup upper-cases the observed literal. The literal is preserved as written rather than folded, because severity-map.md reports observed literals with per-literal row counts and upper-casing it here would misreport a literal the tool never wrote. The record also carries unscored 'true' and no CVSS block, and neither changes the outcome: a mapped label needs no score.

severity_policy.the_rejected_records_contribute_no_liter: The first rejected record carries severity CRITICAL and the second carries no severity member but a cvssv3 baseScore of 7.5. Neither reaches severity.resolve and neither is fed to the LiteralTally, so no literal from them can appear in severity-map.md against rows the dataset does not contain. The second is also the only record in the whole fixture that would have selected a score entry naming both a source and a version ('NVD:cvssv3', '3.1'), which is exactly why severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version is 0 here: the classification order decided it, and a 1 in that counter would mean step 5 had run for a record step 4 rejected.
severity_policy.never_absent: severity_norm is absent on no row. severity_native is absent on no row either -- every emitted record carries a severity member -- so severity_basis_no_vocabulary, the only path setting severity_native null, is 0.
severity_policy.unmapped_literals: None. Every literal on an emitted row is either a mapped label or a bandable number in 0.0-10.0, so severity_basis_unmapped_literal is 0.

in_scope_surface.statement: This tool's only in-scope surface at the pin is the vendored web bundles under core/src/main/resources: 30 .js and 10 .css, 40 files, counted on the pinned tree at 59b8a4489c878fa3a9aa6b7fbae760f2fc80eb9d. Rows 0 and 1 are two of them, and they are the only two in_scope true rows here.
in_scope_surface.example: core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/jquery.cookies.2.2.0.min.js -- row 1, in_scope true, matched glob core/src/main/**
in_scope_surface.the_manifest_in_scope: core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json is in scope by the same glob and appears in this fixture as dependency 7. It contributes no row, because it carries no vulnerabilities key -- not because of its scope. It is 5 lines and 80 bytes, holding a name, a license and "type": "module", with no dependencies block and no lockfile beside it, which is the whole reason the twelve authoritative roots resolve zero dependency manifests and this tool reported zero findings over them.
in_scope_surface.what_this_provisioning_actually_resolved: harness/artifacts/raw/dependency-check.json carries 32 dependencies -- 31 .js files (the 30 under core/src/main/resources plus sql/core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/sql/execution/ui/static/spark-sql-viz.js) and that one package.json -- with zero vulnerabilities and zero packages among them. No .css file became a dependency at all. The 40-file figure above is the in-scope bundle surface on disk; the 32 is what the tool resolved from it. Two different measurements, both stated, neither substituted for the other.
in_scope_surface.no_scope_judgement: Recorded as a property of the scope, exactly as AAP 0.3.2 requires: the allowlist is not widened to give this tool something to resolve, and zero manifests in scope is a fact to report rather than a condition to fix.

corroboration.note: oss-scan-results/findings.json holds 9,433 rows and none of them is a dependency-check row: the tool reported zero findings over the twelve authoritative roots, so there is nothing in the committed dataset to compare these six rows against. The absence is stated rather than papered over -- these rows rest on the fixture and the authored contracts alone, which is what AAP 0.6.2 asks of a hand-verified expected file in any case. The scope fact behind the zero is reported in oss-scan-results/tool-status.md, not here.
corroboration.sibling_agreement: Four of these six rows are records the positive sibling also covers, and this file's values for them agree with oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/expected/dependency-check.rows.json field for field: row 0 is that file's row 0, row 1 its row 1, row 2 its row 4 and row 3 its row 7. Rows 4 and 5 are new here, since both archive dependencies are. That is a consistency check between two hand-derived files rather than corroboration from a run, and it is worth stating for exactly that reason: the four shared rows are unchanged by the defect introduced into a fifth record's dependency.

rows.message: Bootstrap contains a cross-site scripting weakness in the carousel component: the data-slide and data-slide-to attributes are written into the document without neutralizing markup, so a page that renders attacker-influenced attribute values can execute script in the browsing context of the page.

The cookie accessor evaluates a stored cookie value as structured data before returning it, so a cookie written by another document on the same registrable domain can influence the object the caller receives.
The glob prefix parser backtracks on a pattern containing many nested braces, so a long crafted pattern costs time superlinear in its length.
Parsing an XML document containing many digits in a numeric character reference takes time superlinear in the length of the reference, so a small document can occupy the parser for a long time.
The temporary directory helper creates a directory readable by every account on the host, so data a caller writes through it is exposed to other local users.
Reading a crafted serialized value through the collection utilities reserves capacity from a size field the input controls, so a short input can exhaust the heap.

package_coordinate_source.note: The tiebreak row. Both packages[] entries carry a pkg: URL; the lexicographically smallest of the pooled candidates wins, which is the entry at index 1 rather than index 0.

row_derivations.severity_derivation: No mapped label exists, so the number is banded on its own: 5.300000190734863 falls in 4.0-6.9 and bands Medium, and severity_native is its one-decimal rendering '5.3'. The entry names source 'label' and no version because the value came from the severity member rather than from a versioned CVSS block, which is why this row does not increment severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version.
row_derivations.reported_path_form: filesystem-absolute: the root followed by dev/package-lock.json. A virtual dependency still reports the manifest it was read out of, which is a real file on disk.
row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: the name 'sonatype-2022-6438' is an OSS Index advisory identifier and is not CVE-shaped
row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: dev/package-lock.json matches none of the twelve globs. One of the pin's three real lockfiles, legitimately reachable by a dependency-oriented scanner, kept with in_scope false and counted under rows_out_of_scope.

row_derivations.cvss_agreement: cvssv3.baseScore 6.5, baseSeverity MEDIUM -- bands Medium, agreeing with the label that governed
row_derivations.reported_path_form: filesystem-absolute: the root followed by docs/Gemfile.lock
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: the single cwes entry is the NVD placeholder 'NVD-CWE-noinfo', from which no numeric identifier can be read. The field is absent rather than carrying a fabricated 'CWE-noinfo', the entry is counted under cwe_entries_without_identifier, and the row is counted under cwe_absent -- one traversal reporting both numbers so they cannot disagree.

row_derivations.cvss_agreement: cvssv3.baseScore 7.1, baseSeverity HIGH -- bands High, agreeing with the label that governed
row_derivations.reported_path_form: filesystem-absolute AND concatenated: the container path with the member joined onto it by a '/' and no separator, exactly the shape dependency_check.prepare_file_path exists for
row_derivations.path_note: prepare_file_path inserts the single '!' at the first segment whose extension names a container -- '…/spark-network-common_2.13-4.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar' -- and paths.py then relativizes the container and serializes <container>!<member>. Without the split the coordinate would relativize into an ordinary-looking path naming a file that is not on disk. Counted once under archive_references_split.

cwe_source.rule: ascending numeric identifier: 379 < 552. Producer order lists CWE-552 first, so an implementation taking the first entry would emit the other value -- which is why the ordering is stated rather than left to the array.

row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: An archive member is never in scope: paths.in_scope applies the non-filesystem rule before any glob is tested. Independently, the container's own segments match no glob either -- it sits under common/network-common/target/, not common/network-common/src/main/ -- so both reasons agree here. They are recorded separately because the kind rule is the one that decides, and a fixture whose container did sit under a glob would separate them.

row_derivations.cvss_agreement: cvssv3.baseScore 5.9, baseSeverity MEDIUM -- bands Medium, agreeing with the label that governed
row_derivations.reported_path_form: filesystem-absolute and concatenated, as row 4, but under /root/.m2/repository -- the primed Maven local repository, which is outside the scan root
row_derivations.path_note: The container relativizes to ../../root/.m2/repository/com/google/guava/guava/18.0/guava-18.0.jar and the ../ segments are PRESERVED, never normalized away -- the SARIF 2.1.0 errata amendment to section 3.10.2, which paths.py applies to every shape rather than to SARIF alone. The emitted value is still relative, so the no-absolute-path assertion in emit.py holds: expressing an out-of-tree coordinate does not require an absolute path.
row_derivations.out_of_scope_reason: An archive member is never in scope, and this one's container is outside the root as well. The row is kept and counted -- AAP 0.8.3 is explicit that an individual out-of-tree coordinate from a correctly targeted runner is a legitimate coordinate and never evidence of a wrong scan root; only evidence about the runner establishes that.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and the dependency_index / vulnerability_index pair name the same record. The pair is carried as well because it is what the adapter puts in record_identity, so a test can match on either without deriving one from the other.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_ABSENT_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES. See rejection_class above for why this is absent_path and not the unresolvable_path the fixture's slug names.
rejections.reported_file_path_note: The empty string exactly as the fixture carries it, quoted rather than described, because the whole classification turns on it being empty rather than merely unhelpful.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, package coordinate. Steps 1 to 3 pass: the record is an object, its name is a usable string and its description is a usable string. Step 4 rejects.
rejections.steps_never_reached: Step 5 never runs, so the record's formable coordinate pkg:npm/jquery@3.7.1 is never taken and no coordinate counter moves for it. Severity, cwe, cve, path-kind and in_scope are likewise never evaluated, so this record's CRITICAL literal reaches neither the severity counters nor severity-map.md.
rejections.expected_detail: the record carries no the enclosing dependencies[].filePath value, so it names no location; path is not an optional field
rejections.expected_detail_note: Quoted verbatim rather than reworded. paths.resolve_recorded_path composes it as f'the record carries no {tool_base.record_path_field or "path"} value, so it names no location; path is not an optional field', and runner-metadata.json records dependency-check's record_path_field as the phrase 'the enclosing dependencies[].filePath' -- so the doubled article is the composition of a real metadata value and is preserved as written. A test asserting a reworded detail would be asserting against a string the module does not produce.
rejections.record_identity_note: The adapter supplies dependency_index, vulnerability_index, fileName and filePath before step 1 and adds name once step 2 has established it; the resolver adds reported_path with the value it was handed. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and nothing from the record's body.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no path to put in the row. path is never absent from a row, so a record naming no location cannot become one, and nothing here supplies a coordinate for it.

rejections.locator_note: The second record under the SAME dependency, and the reason this fixture's rejection count is two. Nothing about the dependency is evaluated twice: the path is read per record, because the record is the unit.
rejections.classification_step: step 4, as rejection 0. Steps 1 to 3 pass on this record too -- it is an object with a usable name and a usable description.
rejections.steps_never_reached: This record carries no severity member at all but does carry cvssv3 baseScore 7.5 and cvssv2 score 5.0, so had it become a row it would have been the ONLY record in this fixture to select a score entry naming both a source and a version ('NVD:cvssv3', '3.1') and the only one to increment severity_selected_score_with_source_and_version. Step 4 rejects it first, which is why that counter is 0 -- the clearest evidence in this fixture that the classification order is doing real work rather than being decorative.
rejections.expected_detail: the record carries no the enclosing dependencies[].filePath value, so it names no location; path is not an optional field
rejections.expected_detail_note: Byte-identical to rejection 0's detail: the sub-reason describes the path, which is the same empty value for both records. The two rejections are distinguished by their record_identity, not by their prose.
rejections.not_a_duplicate_of_rejection_0: Two rejections under one dependency are two records, not one counted twice, and they are not deduplicated -- AAP 0.3.2 forbids deduplication in either direction. They name different advisories (CVE-2020-11023 and CVE-2020-11022) and differ in their vulnerability_index.

dependencies_contributing_no_record.reason: The dependency carries no vulnerabilities key at all, so it contributes zero records to the count unit. Not a rejection and not an error: a dependency is not a record, and most of the scanned surface has no vulnerability. Counted under dependencies_without_vulnerabilities_array, which is 1.
dependencies_contributing_no_record.in_scope_had_it_produced_a_record: true -- the path matches core/src/main/**. The scope of a dependency that produces no record is stated here rather than left implied, so a reader does not read its absence from rows as an out-of-scope decision.
dependencies_contributing_no_record.the_file_itself: 5 lines and 80 bytes at the pin, holding a name, a license and "type": "module", with no dependencies block and no lockfile beside it. It is the only manifest-shaped file inside the twelve authoritative roots, and its emptiness is the reason the dependency-oriented tools resolved nothing in scope.
dependencies_contributing_no_record.path_resolution_never_attempted: Step 4 is never reached for this dependency because no record under it is ever built, so its filePath is not resolved and no path counter moves for it.
